questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) An organization intends to link all its branches within a town in a network for better communication and sharing of resources.

(i) Based on geographical scope, state the network type that can be setup by the organisation. Give a reason for your answer. (2 marks)

(ii) Given that the computers within each branch are linked in a star topology. Sketch and label the layout of devices in the network with four computers. (4 marks)

(iii) Give two other network topologies that can be used by the organization. Justify your answer (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Network type (2 marks).** A **MAN (Metropolitan Area Network)**. Reason: the branches are spread over one town, so the network covers an area larger than a single building (LAN) but much smaller than a country or the world (WAN).

**(ii) Star topology with four computers (4 marks)**

![fig-2](gce-ol-computer-science-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_2.png)

Marking points: four computers drawn and labelled (1); a central device (hub or switch) drawn and labelled (1); each computer linked to the central device by its own cable, with no link between computers (2). If one cable breaks only that computer is cut off, and a new computer is added simply by connecting it to the hub or switch.

**(iii) Two other topologies with justification (4 marks, 2 marks each)**

Any two of the following:

- **Bus topology:** all the computers are connected to a single main cable (backbone). It is cheap and easy to install because it uses little cable, and it is suitable for a small number of branches.
- **Ring topology:** each computer is connected to two neighbours so that the cable forms a closed loop and the data travels round the ring in one direction. It gives every computer an equal chance to send data and there are few collisions.
- **Mesh topology:** every computer is linked to the others by its own cable, so there are several paths for the data; it is very reliable (if one link fails the data uses another path), but the cabling is expensive.
- **Tree topology:** several star networks are joined to a main backbone; it is easy to extend, which suits an organisation with many branches.

(b) Figure 1 shows a four-level pyramid model of types of information system.

![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_1.png)

(i) Copy and complete the pyramid using the following categories of systems placed in their correct positions: (4 marks)

*Executive Information System (EIS), Decision Support System (DSS), and Management Information System (MIS)*

[You may use the abbreviations as indicated]

(ii) Briefly explain the main purpose of the different categories of information system in the pyramid.

- Executive information system (2 marks)
- Decision support system (2 marks)
- Management information system (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Completed pyramid (4 marks)**

![fig-3](gce-ol-computer-science-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_3.png)

From the top to the bottom: **EIS** (top level), then **DSS**, then **MIS**, and the **Transaction processing system (TPS)** at the base (4 marks: 1 for each of the three positions placed correctly, and 1 for the pyramid copied correctly).

**(ii) Purpose of each category (2 marks each)**

- **Executive information system (EIS):** gives senior managers (the executives) a summary of the most important internal and external information, in the form of graphs, trends and dashboards, to support long-term strategic decisions about the whole organisation.
- **Decision support system (DSS):** helps managers to take decisions on problems that are not routine. It analyses data with models and lets the manager test "what if" situations to compare possible solutions.
- **Management information system (MIS):** takes the data collected by the transaction processing system and summarises it into regular reports (sales, stock, payroll, for example) that middle managers use to monitor, control and plan the daily work of the organisation.
